description: The THIRD answer policy.why gives (D10/SEC-033): `unimplemented: true` is the field an app branches on when the binary itself cannot decide, because a registered type's evaluator has not landed yet. It shares the "refused: " prefix with a real denial and nothing else in the sentence distinguishes the two, so a client that parses prose has already collapsed "nobody can answer this yet" into "a rule refused you" — the exact P31 collapse T11 exists to make unrepresentable. This fixture is what puts the field in ui/src/proto/contract.ts (protogen is fixture-derived); without it the generated type carries only {allowed, sentence} and every reader falls back to startsWith. The scenario is the ONLY reachable one: all seven types are registered (six of them as D10 stubs), so Evaluate's unregistered branch cannot be reached from the socket, and sawUnimplemented needs a live, target-matching row OF THAT TYPE — here a stored operator Deny `ban-force-push` (command_access, target agent:boss) that the stub evaluator refuses to decide. `allowed` is false here and MUST be: refusing rather than permitting is the whole D10 claim, so an answer that admits it cannot decide while also permitting is not a shape this wire carries.

result.sentence: refused: agent:boss · command_access has no evaluator yet · refusing rather than permitting (D10)
